titre: Wave Race Blue Storm : le jeu de lancement de la GameCube refait surface pour les abonnés Nintendo Switch Online
chapo: Troisième et dernier volet de la franchise, Wave Race : Blue Storm est de retour aujourd'hui dans le cadre de l'abonnement Nintendo Switch Online + Pack additionnel.
extrait: Aux côtés de Luigi's Mansion et Super Monkey Ball, Wave Race : Blue Storm est l'un des trois titres qui ont accompagné le lancement de la GameCube dans toutes les régions du monde. C'était au début du siècle et la franchise de motomarine de Nintendo n'a plus donné signe de vie depuis, après un premier jet sur Game Boy (1992) et Nintendo 64 (1996). Ce Wave Race : Blue Storm représente donc le titre le plus abouti de la série tant en matière de technologie que de contenu. Le jeu servait d'ailleurs de vitrine technique avec sa gestion physique des vagues et de la transparence de l'eau, sans oublier une météo qui peut changer au milieu de la course et faire basculer les conditions de navigation (visibilité, niveau de l'eau, hauteur des vagues). Le pilotage demande de négocier les virages serrés avec les gâchettes L et R et de conserver sa jauge de turbo en slalomant entre les bouées et en réalisant des figures aériennes grâce aux tremplins et aux vagues. On retrouve également la possibilité de jouer jusqu'à quatre en écran scindé. On ne va pas se mentir, vous ne lisez Gamekult gratuitement que parce que la publicité paye nos salaires à votre place. titre: Nintendo Switch Online Adds Another GameCube Classic
chapo: Nintendo just added the 2001 jetski racer Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack library.
extrait: Nintendo Switch Online's expansive library of retro games is a treasure trove of nostalgic experiences, and it just got a little bit better. That's because the 2001 GameCube racing game Wave Race: Blue Storm has just been added to the Nintendo Switch Online Plus Expansion Pack library. With the chilly season fast approaching, it's the perfect excuse for a little tropical getaway from the comfort of your couch. While I often think of Wave Race as a series that got its start on the Nintendo 64, the first Wave Race actually came out all the way back in 1992 for the Game Boy. The N64 version marked a big leap forward with fully 3D environments, and Wave Race: Blue Storm goes a step further, thanks to the addition of unique weather conditions to mix up the action. Wave heights and visibility will vary depending on conditions, which can be sunny, foggy, rainy, or choppy. In addition to the weather, there are also hazards to keep an eye out for on each course, like leaping killer whales or trees falling into your path after being struck by lightning. Blue Storm has an eclectic mix of courses too, like a Venice-inspired city, a frosty blue glacier, and a jungle river surrounded by ancient ruins. There's even one level where you bust through an intricate stained-glass window. Take that, church! Blue Storm includes five modes for your sporting pleasure. Championship mode is the core single-player experience, where you'll go head-to-head with seven other riders across four courses, doing three laps on each one. Time Attack mode is exactly what it sounds like: a way to familiarize yourself with one course and winnow down your lap times. In Stunt Mode, you'll need to perform sick tricks and jumps across courses full of ramps and rings instead of simply getting to the finish fastest. Multiplayer provides couch co-op fun for up to four players, while Free Roam lets you explore the courses without any time pressure. November marks the 25th anniversary of the GameCube's 2001 debut, and Wave Race: Blue Storm was one of its launch titles. It was the third-best-selling launch title for the platform in North America, behind Luigi's Mansion and Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader. Sadly, Nintendo hasn't revisited the series since, scrapping plans for a Wii installment that would have used both the Wiimote and the Balance Board peripheral. titre: Nintendo Switch Online Just Got a Long-Awaited Update, Alongside Another GameCube Classic
chapo: GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
extrait: GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature. The Nintendo Classic apps have a border gradient that until now you couldn't remove — and it's something that's proven a bugbear from fans who want a cleaner look. For now, only the GameCube app has the option to simply have clear black borders instead, though it seems likely the other console apps will follow. Or, maybe this is something only the technical power of Switch 2 can pull off? "Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves!" reads an official blurb for the game. "Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms... Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!" Wave Race: Blue Storm becomes the 12th GameCube title available on Switch 2 via the Expansion Pack subscription service, following the previous additions of Chibi-Robo!, F-Zero GX, Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, Luigi's Mansion, Super Mario Strikers, Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, SoulCalibur 2, Star Fox Adventures, Super Mario Sunshine, The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker and Wario World.
